issues.description: The solution introduces an extra constructor parameter (age: Int) in Developer.init that does not appear in the problem statement or the template. Additionally, the solution's Client calls the two-parameter initializer (name, monthsOfSwiftExperience) while the solution's Developer.init requires three parameters, creating an internal mismatch that will prevent the code from compiling and contradicts the intended initializer signature described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Developer initializer signature consistent across all artifacts. Either remove the extraneous age: Int parameter from solution/Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift so the init is init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) (matching the template and problem statement), or update the problem statement and all uses (including Client.swift and the template) to include the age parameter. Preferably remove the age parameter in the solution to align with the exercise specification.

issues.description: The Developer initializer signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template expect an initializer taking (name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?), but the solution’s Developer class adds an extra parameter 'age' in its initializer. This creates a mismatch between the expected instantiation (used in the solution's Client and described in the problem) and the actual solution class API, causing confusion about how to construct a Developer.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Developer initializer across all artifacts. Remove the extra 'age' parameter from the solution's Developer.init so it matches init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?), or alternatively update the problem statement and template to include the 'age' parameter and adjust Client calls accordingly. Prefer keeping init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) to match the exercise description.
